claims.claim_text: The indexed Daniel C. Buchanan is a high-confidence match to Daniel Crump Buchanan, the Japan specialist documented at the OSS Japanese desk and in OSS/FESI correspondence.
claims.evidence_excerpt: During World War Two he worked at the Japanese desk of the U.S. Office of Strategic Services
claims.evidence_paraphrase: An institutional finding aid identifies Daniel Crump Buchanan at the OSS Japanese desk; a government historical database independently lists Daniel C. Buchanan in OSS/FESI correspondence.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence: exact first and last name, matching middle initial expanded to Crump, Japanese specialization, and two independent OSS contexts agree.
claims.temporal_assessment: The corroborating OSS documents date from October 1944 through July 1945; the finding aid separately places his missionary and teaching work before wartime OSS service.
claims.match_notes: The indexed row has no private identifier, so the match remains high confidence rather than confirmed and Box 90 review is still warranted.

claims.claim_text: Before his documented OSS work, Daniel Crump Buchanan had served as a Presbyterian minister, missionary, and teacher in Japan.

claims.evidence_paraphrase: Washington and Lee's finding aid dates his Presbyterian ordination to 1920, then places missionary and teaching work in Japan before his wartime OSS Japanese-desk work.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence identity supported by the finding aid and independent exact-middle-initial OSS/FESI correspondence.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar, but not proven to be the immediate pre-OSS affiliation or the last civilian employer; no exact end date or employing institution is named.
claims.match_notes: The relationship is professional affiliation, not a named employer. No mission board, church, school, or college is inferred.
